text: 🇲🇽🇨🇺 "We deployed 820 personnel in emergency response brigades to bring aid to sister countries, Cuba and Venezuela." — Admiral Raymundo Pedro Morales Ángeles, Secretary of the Navy, Veracruz Aboard three ships, the Navy carried more than 4,000 tonnes of food, bottled water, water purification plants and medical supplies this year. The admiral called it "defense in depth in its most human expression." The Navy guards more than 11,000 km of coastline and over 3 million km² of maritime zones. This year naval aviation turned 100 and Plan Marina, its disaster-response plan, turned 60.
banner: NAVY: 4,000 TONNES OF AID TO CUBA, VENEZUELA

text: 🇲🇽⚓ "Veracruz is four times heroic, because at different moments in our history its people rose up to defend the homeland against foreign forces." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, 205th anniversary of the Mexican Navy, Veracruz She named them at the ceremony for the Navy's 205th anniversary, held in the port: 1825, against the last Spanish stronghold at San Juan de Ulúa; 1838, during the first French intervention; 1847 and 1914, against the United States invasion. "Civilians, soldiers, sailors, young cadets showed again and again that the defense of the homeland does not depend only on weapons." In April 1914, Naval School cadets resisted the US landing; Lt. José Azueta and cadet Virgilio Uribe died defending the port.

🇲🇽🥑 <u>No Labor Certificate, No Avocado Exports</u>

Since October 1, Mexican avocado packers need the Labor Certificate for Agro-Exports, which proves they pay IMSS social security for their workers, to ship under the program agreed with the United States. A zero-deforestation certificate will cover every export shipment, whether it goes to the US, Europe or Asia.

Volume is booming. Exports rose from 751,000 to 1 million tonnes between January and August, up 33.7%, El Economista reports. Prices did not hold, though: export value fell 44.5% to $1.479 billion as the average price dropped from 70 to 26 pesos a kilo.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Customs Reform Puts 2 Trillion Pesos Under Guard</u>

Close to 2 trillion pesos a year flows through Mexican customs via virtual operations, deferrals and exemptions. Morena deputy Claudia Rivera Vivanco says the reform to the Customs Law will close those channels with technology and no new taxes, and stop abuses by transnational companies.

The reform cuts the value gap that triggers a presumption of undervaluation from 50% to 20%. Rivera wants customs to become "a political lever for industrialization" tied to Plan México, not only a tool for collection and control.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Cuba's Vice Minister Thanks Mexico in San Lázaro</u>

Cuban Vice Foreign Minister Carlos Fernández de Cossío, with Ambassador Eugenio Martínez, met the Mexico-Cuba Friendship Group in Mexico's Chamber of Deputies. He thanked Mexican society and the Mexican government for standing with the island at a time when "Cuba lives under a multidimensional aggression" from the United States.

Morena deputies spoke of a "moral obligation" to back President Sheinbaum's support for Cuba. A Cuban fuel ship the US intercepted a month ago is still sitting in Puerto Progreso.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Arizona High Schoolers Are Arming Mexico's Cartels</u>

A New York Times investigation from Phoenix followed four teenagers, ages 16 to 19, who buy, steal or scam their way into pistols and AR-15s and sell them to cartel intermediaries through encrypted WhatsApp groups and Telegram channels. They clear $4,000 to $5,000 a month.

Mexican authorities estimate up to 500,000 guns are smuggled south from the United States every year. Washington calls the cartels terrorists, and its own kids are running their supply chain.
banner: GUNS TO CARTELS: US TEENS SELLING

🇲🇽📈 <u>Yucatán refinances debt, frees federal revenue for public works</u>

Yucatán's government, led by Morena's Joaquín Díaz Mena, restructured a 2019 Banamex loan on September 29. The deal cuts the rate by 14 basis points, keeps the state's lowest spread (0.25%) and saves 29 million pesos over the life of the credit, El Financiero reports.

The share of federal revenue pledged as collateral drops from 13.5% to 8.8%, and the freed money goes to public investment. HR Ratings has Yucatán at AA+ with a positive outlook, and IMCO's 2026 competitiveness index moved it from 10th to 7th, its best position since the ranking began.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>AIFA +9.6%: the "white elephant" keeps growing</u>

Mexico's airports moved 128.3 million passengers from January to August 2026: 86.8 million domestic and 41.5 million international. August alone hit 16.8 million, up 2.7% year on year.

Among the 15 busiest terminals, the growth leaders were Querétaro (+11.7%), AIFA (+9.6%) and Mérida (+7%).

The opposition spent years calling AIFA a white elephant. It's now the second-fastest-growing major airport in the country.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"One flag, one people, one homeland"</u>

Sheinbaum says once state congresses ratify the reform barring dual nationals from the presidency, governorships and Mexico City's top office, it takes effect immediately. She added that Morena must explain naming US-born Jasmine Bugarín as its Nayarit coordinator. Candidates, she said, need "one flag, one people, one homeland."

Two days later, Bugarín was at the US consulate in Guadalajara starting the paperwork to renounce her US citizenship: "Mexico is my homeland."

The rule applied to Morena first.
banner: ONE FLAG: BUGARÍN QUITS US CITIZENSHIP

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Health tenders: Mexican suppliers' volume up 301%</u>

Mexico's Health Secretariat closed its 2027-2028 medical-supplies tender: 12.569 billion pesos for 646 million pieces, 94.5% of the volume requested.

The story is who's making them. Codes awarded to Mexican industry jumped from 90 to 173 (+92%), and pieces from 148 million to 594.6 million, a 301% increase.

In 2019, La Jornada reported that just ten companies had concentrated the health sector's medicine purchases under the previous government. Now public money is buying national production.
